question: "Rajendra I" was the son of which chola ruler?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajaraja I**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Rajendra I**, one of the most prominent rulers of the Chola dynasty, was the son of **Rajaraja I**, the great Chola emperor who laid the foundation for the Chola Empire’s expansion and administrative reforms. 
• **Rajaraja I** ruled from **985–1014 CE** and is credited with consolidating and strengthening the Chola dynasty into a formidable empire. 
• Under Rajaraja I’s reign, the Chola Empire witnessed significant territorial expansion, including conquests in Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and parts of South India, which Rajendra I later expanded further. 
• Rajaraja I was instrumental in initiating large-scale temple constructions, including the renowned **Brihadeeswarar Temple** at Thanjavur, which is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. His architectural patronage was a legacy continued by his son, Rajendra I. 
• Rajendra I succeeded his father in **1014 CE** and carried forward his legacy by further expanding the empire to include regions like Southeast Asia and the Gangetic plains. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Rajaraja I’s Achievements:** 
• He established a highly organized and efficient administrative system, dividing the empire into provinces called **mandalams** for better governance. 
• He introduced a systematic revenue collection system and ensured the prosperity of the empire through trade and agriculture. 
• Rajaraja I’s military campaigns led to the annexation of northern Sri Lanka, which he renamed **Mummudi Chola Mandalam**. 
• He was a patron of art and architecture and played a significant role in the development of Dravidian temple architecture. 
• **Rajendra I’s Contributions:** 
• Rajendra I is known for his naval expeditions, particularly the conquest of the **Srivijaya Empire** (modern-day Indonesia and Malaysia), marking the Chola Empire as a maritime power. 
• He built a new capital city called **Gangaikonda Cholapuram** to commemorate his victory over the Ganga dynasty. 
• Under his reign, the Chola Empire became one of the most powerful empires in Asia, with influence spreading across Southeast Asia. 
• Rajendra I also constructed numerous temples and irrigation systems, further strengthening the empire’s infrastructure. 
• **Other Options Explained:** 
• **Vijayalaya:** He was the founder of the Chola dynasty in the 9th century CE, but he was not the father of Rajendra I. 
• **Parantaka Chola I:** He was an earlier ruler of the Chola dynasty (907–950 CE) and a significant figure in its early expansion but not directly related to Rajendra I. 
• **Kulothunga:** He was a later Chola ruler who reigned in the 11th century CE, long after Rajendra I’s time. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Brihadeeswarar Temple:** Built by Rajaraja I, this temple remains a masterpiece of Chola architecture and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. 
• **Chola Navy:** The Chola dynasty developed one of the most powerful navies in ancient India, which played a crucial role in their conquests under Rajendra I. 
• **Trade and Economy:** Both Rajaraja I and Rajendra I encouraged maritime trade, especially in the Indian Ocean region, fostering economic prosperity. 
• **Inscriptional Evidence:** The reigns of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I are well-documented through inscriptions, which provide valuable insights into their governance and achievements.
